factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash flow statement shows operating cash flow increased by 15.0% to EUR 103,131 thousand (103.1 million) in H1 2026.

factual_claims.claim: Consequently, free cash flow advanced by 12.5 percent to EUR 64.1 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash flow statement shows free cash flow increased by 12.5% to EUR 64,099 thousand (64.1 million) in H1 2026.

factual_claims.claim: On the balance sheet, Telia Lietuva transformed its financing position, converting a prior-year net debt balance into a net cash position of minus EUR 4.3 million by late June.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial position and cash flow section states net debt was (EUR 4,255 thousand) as of 30 June 2026, representing a net cash position.

factual_claims.claim: This improved liquidity facilitated a record dividend distribution of EUR 81.6 million, or EUR 0.14 per share, covering the full 2025 fiscal year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Dividends section states EUR 81.6 million (EUR 0.14 per share) was distributed as dividends for the year 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Strategic capital expenditure accelerated substantially, surging 57.9 percent to EUR 37.5 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Capital investments section shows total capital investments increased by 57.9% to EUR 37,458 thousand (37.5 million) in H1 2026.

factual_claims.claim: The majority of investments targeted network modernization and digital infrastructure, including EUR 14.2 million for IT systems and EUR 9.7 million dedicated to spectrum licenses.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Capital investments breakdown shows IT systems and infrastructure at EUR 14,174 thousand (14.2 million) and 5G spectrum licenses at EUR 9,690 thousand (9.7 million) in H1 2026.

factual_claims.claim: A focal point of the period was the acquisition of two 1,500 MHz frequency blocks for nearly EUR 8 million in a national regulatory auction, securing 40 MHz of spectrum specifically optimized for high-speed mobile data transmission.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Capital investments section states: 'In June 2026, the Company acquired two 1,500 MHz frequency blocks for almost EUR 8 million... The Company received the largest share of these frequencies sold – 40 MHz... which will be used for further development of the 5G network.'

factual_claims.claim: The company also secured additional rights to the 2,100 MHz band for EUR 2 million to bolster 5G capacity.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: CEO comment states: 'Along with this achievement, Telia Lietuva also extended its right to use the 2,100 MHz frequency band in another auction, committing to pay another EUR 2 million for this right.'

factual_claims.claim: Concurrently, fiber-optic coverage expanded to 992,000 households nationwide, while plans were initiated for a new data center project requiring up to EUR 26 million in phased investments through 2027.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Capital investments section states: 'By the end of June 2026, the Company had 992 thousand households passed... In 2026, Telia Lietuva commenced construction of a new data center near Vilnius... The Company plans to invest up to EUR 26 million to two initial data center modules... to be completed by the second half of 2027.'

factual_claims.claim: Sustained mobile data traffic growth of approximately 25 percent annually continues to underpin network utilization.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: CEO comment states: 'Mobile data traffic in Lithuania is growing by around 25 per cent annually, one of the fastest growth rates in Europe.'
